title: Dung Beetles Steer by the Milky Way, and Cardboard Hats Proved It

scenes.text: Dung beetles steer by the Milky Way.
They roll a ball of dung in a perfectly straight line, so rivals can't steal it.
Scientists put tiny cardboard hats on them. Without the sky, the beetles wandered in circles.
Their eyes can't see single stars, so they follow the soft glow of the Milky Way itself.
They proved it in a planetarium in Johannesburg.
A beetle with a ball of poop, using the galaxy as a map.

description:
Dung beetles steer by the Milky Way.
A 2013 study in Current Biology showed that South African dung beetles roll their dung balls in straight lines by following the glow of the Milky Way. With cardboard hats blocking the sky, they lost their way.
Could you find your way home by the Milky Way? Comment below.
